item: Exclusive windows that overlap count instead of restoring the flag each found on entry, and the encrypt route no longer sits in the collection restart's retry loop
summary: The read of the final head: a backup export holding the gate while an encryption in place waits for it ends its window first, and the old exit restored the value ITS entry found (False), so collection restarted and the guard's drain ran inside the file swap, then the encryption's own exit set the flag back to True for good (every later drain refused, a later restore not pausing collection). The window now counts (the number open, the value the first one found, whether any of them paused collection): the LAST window out lowers the flag and resumes, a window that begins inside another mints no new run, and the root cause is older than the encryption route (any two windows that overlap without nesting). The encrypt route passes resume_retries=0: its request no longer sleeps up to 19 x 30 s (570 s) in the restart's retry loop after the store is encrypted, with the guard declining every drain meanwhile; the pending-resume watcher takes over. 7 tests on the windows (the overlap that began inside another and ends after it, the window that paused not being the one that resumes, nested exits, one run token for overlapping windows, a flag raised by hand, an exception in one of two, the retry budget passed on) and 2 on the encrypt route (a pass still winding down does not hold the response, a backup window ending during the swap does not free the machine under it); ten mutants killed.
